1 # Offline regression evidence pipeline, contract 3.0
   2 
   3 Repair and extend the provided H3Act project so `python3 main.py` compiles payloads,
   4 replays decoded client events, and audits compressed origin captures. The existing
   5 schema models, FuzzExecutor adapter, and HttpClient form the application, not an
   6 external service. The offline clock is a socket-free coroutine utility. Complete
   7 the byte-program and audit extension and repair integration/lifecycle defects.
   8 Equivalent implementations are accepted; internal algorithms are your choice.
   9 
  10 This model starts after transport delivery/field decoding. It sends no packets,
  11 runs no model, and has no live CDN, QPACK, TLS, SSH, GPU, response cache, or wall-time
  12 simulation. Its receipt encoding below is an audit format, not HTTP/3 wire format.
  13 Diagnostic flags describe this paired recording, not a proof of a real exploit.
  14 
  15 ## Input and domain
  16 
  17 Read exactly one UTF-8 JSON object without a byte-order mark, with surrounding
  18 JSON whitespace allowed.
  19 Reject duplicate keys, invalid UTF-8/JSON, nonfinite numbers (including overflowing
  20 exponents), trailing values, wrong types, unknown/missing keys, or budget violations
  21 with exactly `{"error":"input"}` and exit0. Every input string must encode as
  22 UTF-8; lone Unicode surrogates are invalid. Booleans are not integers. No coercion.
  23 Validate the whole input, including frames/events that ultimately are not used.
  24 Otherwise output the result described below and exit0. Emit JSON only on stdout.
  25 
  26 The root has exactly `seed`, `definitions`, `timeout_ms`, `cases`, `events`, `channels`.
  27 `seed` is 0-64 ASCII letters/digits/underscore/dot/hyphen. `timeout_ms` is an integer
  28 in [1,1000000000]. Names of cases/channels are unique within their kind and use
  29 1-32 of those ASCII characters. Arrays preserve order. Object member order is
  30 irrelevant except for the ordered header mapping described below.
  31 
  32 Budgets are inclusive: raw stdin8MiB; definitions8192; cases2000; channels256;
  33 combined number of case frames + external events + capture parts50000; combined
  34 header pairs in input frames and external events32768; pairs per header block128;
  35 expression source8192 Unicode code points; other template source65536 code points.
  36 Logical byte sequence lengths, channel lengths, receipt lengths, body lengths,
  37 and virtual times are in [0,2^63-1]. Every case's sum of pauses + timeout_ms must
  38 fit this range. At most20000 complete origin requests and40000 complete chunk-size
  39 lines (including zero chunks and lines in an unfinished request) may be examined
  40 across all channels. Count a line in chunk-size position after its CRLF/line-limit
  41 check and before checking the hexadecimal size or suffix; a malformed line
  42 terminator or unfinished line is not counted. These are input-domain budgets, not a scoring objective.
  43 
  44 Compressed captures cover very large objects and repeated boundary probes without
  45 storing their expanded contents. Metadata counts model a batch audit between
  46 experiment rounds; signed64-bit offsets permit sparse capture ranges. Resource
  47 limits support an interactive batch audit and are not a speed ranking. Materialized
  48 traffic volume or the number of discovered diagnostic flags is not a score.
  49 
  50 ## Byte expressions, templates and fingerprints
  51 
  52 `definitions` is an ordered array of `[name, expression]`. Names are distinct,
  53 non-keyword Python identifiers matching `[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,31}`. An expression
  54 can refer only to earlier definitions. The accepted Python expression syntax is:
  55 Unicode string or bytes literals; nonnegative integer literals <=2^63-1; earlier names; parentheses;
  56 concatenation `+` of byte sequences; repetition `*` with one byte sequence and one
  57 integer (either order); and a byte slice `[lo:hi]` with either endpoint optionally
  58 omitted. A final expression must be bytes, never an integer. Slice endpoints are
  59 integer literals, with 0<=lo<=hi<=length; omitted endpoints mean0/length. No negative
  60 index, nonempty slice step, integer arithmetic, boolean, call, attribute,
  61 list, format string or other syntax is supported. AST nesting depth is at most128,
  62 counting the root expression body as depth0 and every AST child edge, including
  63 slice/operator/context nodes. Parentheses do not add AST depth.
  64 Definition sources use CPython3.11 `ast.parse(source, mode="eval")` as supplied,
  65 without whitespace normalization; sources it rejects are invalid. Empty third
  66 slice components (`[lo:hi:]` or `[::]`) are equivalent to an omitted step.
  67 Unicode string literals encode to UTF-8; bytes literals supply their exact bytes
  68 before any byte operation; slices are byte offsets,
  69 even within an encoded character. An empty sequence and zero repetitions are legal.
  70 
  71 Every template is a JSON string. A string starting `{{` and ending `}}` is a whole
  72 expression template: strip those outer markers and surrounding expression whitespace,
  73 then evaluate it. Other strings are UTF-8 literal data, except each occurrence of
  74 `<<random_string>>` is replaced by the first20 lowercase hex characters of SHA256
  75 of the UTF-8 string `seed/coordinate/occurrence`. Occurrences are numbered from0
  76 left to right independently per template. Tokens inside expression string literals
  77 are literal data. Markers embedded in an ordinary literal are not expressions.
  78 Coordinates are exactly:
  79 
  80 - Frame j of case i: `case/i/frame/j/data`; header pair k uses
  81   `case/i/frame/j/h/k/n` for its name and `/v` for its value instead of `/n`.
  82 - External event i: `event/i/data`, or `event/i/h/k/n` and `/v` for headers.
  83 - Capture part j of channel i: `channel/i/part/j/data`.
  84 
  85 All indices in coordinates use unpadded decimal. A fingerprint of bytes b is exactly
  86 `{"n":N,"h":"hhhhhhhhhhhhhhhh"}`: N is byte length and h is the 16-digit lowercase
  87 hex value of sum((b[i]+1)*257^(N-1-i)) modulo2^64. Empty bytes have n0 and all-zero h.
  88 A fingerprint is a requested exact checksum; checksum equality is not asserted
  89 to prove byte equality. Routing-identity comparisons below compare actual bytes.
  90 
  91 ## Cases, frames and external events
  92 
  93 Each case is exactly `{"name":NAME,"frames":[FRAME,...],"expect":EXPECT}`.
  94 EXPECT has exactly `method`, `target`, `host`: nonempty ASCII visible strings
  95 (no whitespace), each at most8192 bytes; method is an HTTP token. This is supplied
  96 intended routing identity for comparison, rather than a hidden inference target.
  97 A token uses ASCII letters, digits and `!#$%&'*+-.^_` plus grave accent, `|~`.
  98 
  99 Frames keep the project model names and spelling:
 100 
 101 | Type | Input fields besides required Type |
 102 | --- | --- |
 103 | `headers` | Exactly one of `headers_kv` (string:string object) or `data_to_transfered` (array of two-string arrays); optional boolean `End_Stream`, default false |
 104 | `data`, `datagram` | Required string `data_to_transfered`; optional boolean `End_Stream`, default true |
 105 | `sleep` | Required integer `Time_to_Stop` in [0,2^63-1]; no End_Stream |
 106 
 107 All other keys are forbidden. Header mapping pairs follow JSON member order; the
 108 list representation also preserves duplicates. Compile each header name/value or
 109 data string as a template. Do not validate HTTP field content in these fuzz frames:
 110 malformed/duplicate pseudo fields are deliberately representable. A sleep consumes
 111 virtual milliseconds, emits no frame and cannot finish a request. A datagram emits
 112 a frame but its End_Stream is ignored. Headers/data with End_Stream=true close
 113 the request send side. Any later non-sleep frame for that stream is a send error
 114 and is not emitted; a sleep after request-end is still permitted.
 115 
 116 All cases start at virtual time0, in case-array order, on one connection. Their
 117 stream IDs are4*i. External events are exactly one of:
 118 
 119 - `{"at":T,"kind":"headers","stream":S,"fields":[[name,value],...],"end":BOOL}`
 120 - `{"at":T,"kind":"data","stream":S,"data":TEMPLATE,"end":BOOL}`
 121 - `{"at":T,"kind":"close"}`
 122 
 123 T is a nonnegative signed64-bit time, S is an integer in [0,2^32-1]. Compile all
 124 event fields/data as templates. The event array may be out of timestamp order.
 125 At equal time, ordering is: all initial case starts first; external events in
 126 input-array order; pause completions in case-array order; timeouts in case-array
 127 order. Frames between awaits are emitted together in source order. There is no
 128 real sleep. A zero pause still yields to same-time external events.
 129 
 130 Each case retains response events on its allocated stream until the first event
 131 with end=true. Unknown streams, later response events, and events for an already
 132 terminal case are ignored. Responses arriving while a case is still sending or
 133 paused must be retained. A case is `ok` when both its frame sequence is exhausted
 134 and a response end has been retained. It is `timeout` at send-finish+timeout_ms
 135 if still awaiting response end; an exactly tied response event wins. A connection
 136 close terminates every nonterminal case as `closed`, including paused senders,
 137 and prevents later emissions. A later close cannot replace an already terminal
 138 result. A send error makes the case `send_error`. State and completion time are
 139 fixed at termination. Accepted response events before that termination remain in
 140 its receipt even when the case closes/times out/errors. A response end alone does
 141 not cancel remaining request frames or pauses.
 142 
 143 ## Client receipts and output case records
 144 
 145 Each emitted action contributes this concatenation to its case's sent receipt:
 146 8-byte big-endian unsigned virtual time,4-byte big-endian stream ID,one ASCII kind
 147 byte,encoded content,and one final byte (1 for end,true;0 otherwise). Kinds are
 148 `H` for sent headers, `D` for data, `G` for datagram. Datagram's final byte is0.
 149 Header content is8-byte pair count,then for each pair:8-byte name length,name bytes,
 150 8-byte value length,value bytes. Data content is8-byte data length followed by data.
 151 Accepted received events use exactly the same format with lowercase `h`/`d`.
 152 Receipts concatenate in their case's actual emission/acceptance order.
 153 
 154 The result root is exactly `{"cases":[CASE_RECORD,...],"channels":[CHANNEL_RECORD,...]}`.
 155 Case records follow input case order and have exactly:
 156 `name`, `stream`, `state`, `at`, `frames`, `request_frames`, `payload_bytes`, `sent`,
 157 `received`, `response_frames`, `response_body`, `origin_count`, `flags`.
 158 `at` is completion time. frames counts emitted non-sleep actions; request_frames
 159 counts emitted headers/data actions. payload_bytes sums header name/value lengths
 160 and data/datagram lengths, excluding receipt framing. sent/received are fingerprints
 161 of their receipts. response_frames counts accepted external headers/data events;
 162 response_body fingerprints only accepted external DATA bytes in order.
 163 Origin count and flags are defined below. All counts/offsets/times are JSON integers,
 164 excluding booleans. No extra output keys, duplicate keys, nonfinite values, extra
 165 JSON values or nonzero exit status are accepted. Object key order is free.
 166 
 167 ## Origin channels and request framing
 168 
 169 Each channel is exactly `{"name":NAME,"parts":[{"case":OWNER,"data":TEMPLATE},...]}`.
 170 OWNER is a case name or null. Parts concatenate in order; zero-length parts are
 171 legal. Owners are recording provenance labels, not parsed Host/User-Agent fields.
 172 Channels are independent byte streams. Parse consecutive HTTP/1.1 requests from
 173 byte0. Fully framed requests contribute records; stop at the first syntax error
 174 or unfinished request, retaining earlier records. Byte offsets are channel-relative
 175 and half-open. A channel error is exactly `{"kind":"syntax"|"incomplete","offset":R}`,
 176 where R is the start of the first uncommitted request. An empty/fully consumed
 177 channel has error null.
 178 
 179 Lines require CRLF, with at most8192 bytes before CRLF. If no LF has arrived and the remaining prefix has at most8193 bytes,
 180 it is incomplete; line content is checked only when LF arrives. A bare LF or an LF beyond the line limit is syntax. A prefix
 181 longer than8193 bytes without LF is syntax. A request line is exactly
 182 `METHOD SP TARGET SP HTTP/1.1 CRLF`; METHOD is a nonempty token and TARGET is
 183 nonempty ASCII visible bytes excluding SP. No alternate whitespace separator.
 184 
 185 Header lines are `NAME:value CRLF`, followed by an empty line. NAME is an ASCII
 186 token, case-insensitive for framing rules. Values allow SP..tilde and HTAB only;
 187 strip outer SP/HTAB, preserve all interior bytes. No folding. Initial block size,
 188 including request line and final empty line,is at most65536 bytes and128 fields.
 189 Block size/count checks occur after each complete line; an unterminated line
 190 is governed by the line-prefix rule above.
 191 
 192 No Content-Length or Transfer-Encoding means zero body, regardless of method.
 193 Every Content-Length occurrence contains a nonempty comma-separated list of decimal
 194 unsigned values; trim SP/HTAB per member,permit leading zeros,and require all values
 195 identical and <=2^63-1. A Transfer-Encoding is permitted only as one field with
 196 trimmed case-insensitive value `chunked` and no Content-Length. Conflicts are syntax.
 197 A length body is exactly the declared opaque bytes; bytes resembling requests do
 198 not create new messages. Insufficient bytes mean incomplete.
 199 
 200 Chunked bodies have hexadecimal unsigned size lines with optional `;` and an
 201 uninterpreted suffix of SP..tilde/HTAB. No whitespace in the size,at least one hex
 202 digit,leading zeros allowed,numeric value <=2^63-1. A nonzero chunk has exactly its
 203 size in opaque bytes and then CRLF. A zero size is followed directly by a trailer
 204 field block and final empty line. Trailer block size (excluding zero-size line)
 205 is at most65536 bytes and128 fields; Host,Content-Length,Transfer-Encoding names
 206 are forbidden there. Other duplicates are preserved. A missing body/suffix/trailer
 207 is incomplete. A wrong complete suffix/line/field is syntax. Concatenate only
 208 nonzero chunk DATA for the body fingerprint. Headers/trailers use the same field
 209 rules. The parser's stated limits are this capture-reader policy,not a full HTTP
 210 implementation or a claim that every tolerated request is RFC-conformant.
 211 
 212 ## Origin records and paired evidence flags
 213 
 214 A channel record has exactly `name`, `bytes`, `requests`, `committed`, `error`.
 215 bytes fingerprints the complete concatenated capture. committed contains the count
 216 of complete published requests after each input part,including zero-length parts.
 217 Requests follow byte order. A request record has exactly `start`, `end`, `method`,
 218 `target`, `host`, `host_count`, `headers`, `body`, `trailers`, `framing`, `owner`,
 219 `owners`, `flags`. Method/target are byte fingerprints. If exactly one Host exists,
 220 host fingerprints its trimmed ASCII-lowercased value; otherwise it is empty.
 221 headers/trailers fingerprint their field blocks encoded as8-byte pair count then
 222 8-byte name length,name bytes,8-byte trimmed value length,value bytes per pair,
 223 preserving name spelling and pair order. framing is `none`, `length`, or `chunked`.
 224 body fingerprints the deframed opaque body.
 225 
 226 owner is the provenance label of the request's first byte. owners is an array of
 227 [label,positive byte count] for the complete raw request span,merging equal labels
 228 and ordered by their first occurrence. Raw span includes framing,headers,trailers.
 229 Request flags are a lexicographically sorted set:
 230 
 231 - `unattributed`: owner is null.
 232 - `mixed_owner`: some positive byte of the raw request has a different owner.
 233 - `missing_host`/`multiple_host`: zero/more than one Host field (even identical).
 234 - `identity`: a named owner has any mismatch against its expect: method/target
 235   compare exact bytes,Host must be unique and compares after ASCII case folding.
 236 - `extra`: this is a named owner's second or later request in channel-array order,
 237   then byte order within each channel.
 238 - `unsent`: named owner emitted no headers/data action,even if datagrams were sent.
 239 
 240 origin_count per case counts requests whose first byte has that owner. Case flags
 241 are sorted unique: `missing_origin` if request_frames>0 and count0; `extra_origin`
 242 if count>1; `unsent_origin` if count>0 and request_frames0; `identity` if any owned
 243 request has that flag; `mixed_origin` if any owned request has mixed_owner. These
 244 flags never infer byte equality from checksums and do not label missing client
 245 responses or legitimate origin expansion as vulnerabilities.
 246 
 247 See RUNTIME.md for the complete public development and scored execution profiles.
 248 
 249 ## Local development wrapper (evidence infrastructure)
 250 
 251 
 252 Local development uses a separate nonroot, chrooted outer process to run the
 253 actual public checker or an opaque installation wrapper. Its limits are 120 s
 254 wall time; 120/121 s soft/hard CPU per process; 2 GiB address space per process;
 255 8 MiB stack; 128 file descriptors; process-count rlimit 64 per UID; 64 MiB per
 256 file; and zero core dumps. The outer stdout/stderr caps are 16 MiB/1 MiB.
 257 It uses the same published scratch path, reset, 0.25 s sampling, 1 GiB/50,000-entry
 258 emergency policy, accounting limitations, and infrastructure-error/no-score
 259 outcome described above. Network access is denied and CPU affinity is unchanged.
 260 
 261 Ordinary process creation and same-UID child signaling are allowed in this outer
 262 profile so the checker and opaque installer can launch, stop, and reap children.
 263 Namespace creation remains forbidden: namespace clone flags are rejected,
 264 unshare/setns are denied, and clone3 returns ENOSYS. These outer limits concern
 265 local development evidence infrastructure and impose no candidate algorithm
 266 requirement. Each scored translation invocation, including the public checker's
 267 bounded translation child, continues to use the scored limits above and their
 268 child/thread/signaling denials. The outer profile changes no input semantics,
 269 output schema, serialization, scoring behavior, or submission interface.
